messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test case "testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass" fails due to issues around setting a custom geometric mean implementation in SummaryStatistics and verifying its value. The test creates an instance of SummaryStatistics, sets its geometric mean implementation to a new GeometricMean object, adds some values, and then asserts that the result from getGeometricMean matches the evaluation of a standalone GeometricMean on the same data.

From the SummaryStatistics code, the setGeoMeanImpl method simply assigns a new StorelessUnivariateStatistic instance to geoMeanImpl after a checkEmpty() call. The getGeometricMean method returns the result of geoMeanImpl.getResult(), and addValue calls increment on geoMeanImpl only if it is not the default GeometricMean implementation.

The current bug report describes a possibly related but separate issue with setVarianceImpl causing getStandardDeviation to return NaN. The standard deviation is calculated as the square root of getVariance, which returns the varianceImpl.getResult(), and setVarianceImpl similarly replaces the variance computation object. This suggests a similar design where implementations can be replaced, but if the replacement implementation does not behave correctly or is not incremented correctly, the returned variance could be NaN.

The failing test's issue might be related to how the replaceable implementations are incremented and if they are correctly updated during addValue calls. In the test, a new GeometricMean is set, but then the added values may or may not properly increment this new object depending on the logic in addValue. In the code of addValue, geoMeanImpl.increment(value) is called only if geoMeanImpl is not an instance of GeometricMean, which looks counterintuitive if the intent is to increment any replacement implementation. This can cause the new GeometricMean to not be incremented at all, resulting in getResult() returning an uninitialized value (likely NaN or zero), causing assertion failure.

Similarly, the bug report on variance suggests that setting a new variance implementation without properly incrementing it causes getStandardDeviation to return NaN, again because the variance implementation never receives the values to update its internal state. This parallels the geometric mean problem.

In summary, the bug arises because when users replace the default implementation (be it geometric mean or variance), the system does not correctly increment the substituted implementation with new values. This causes the statistical results to be either NaN or incorrect because the implementation is never updated.

To fix, the logic in addValue should be checked so that whenever a user replaces an implementation with a new one, that new object is incremented with all added values, instead of relying on instanceof checks excluding the default instance.

This diagnosis connects the test failure and the current bug report with the underlying mechanism of replacement implementations in SummaryStatistics and their improper updating during addValue.

Suggested fixes should focus on the addValue method and possibly on setGeoMeanImpl and setVarianceImpl to ensure states are reset or incremented correctly after replacement.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
